content: When I am refactoring a file to reduce imports, sometimes the file has some public auxiliary results which depend on some of the imports I am trying to reduce. In this case, if I deprecate these auxiliary results, then I will have to keep around the imports used to state and prove them, which means the imports do not get reduced. How should I handle such declarations?

In general, would move them to a new file in the Deprecated folder.

Or (this is something to be discussed with the maintainers, though) if they are called _aux something and have not been used in any project you know of, my own claim is it is okay to delete them without deprecation.
how would this apply to my PR #36239, for example?
